title: Hot flash in the boardroom — the written ask (Fawcett 2022)
caption:
Hot flash mid-presentation. She thought she was the problem.
1 in 10 UK women left a job over menopause symptoms (Fawcett, 2022). Ask HR in writing: desk fan, flex start.
Send this to her. Told work yet?
www.aiforheratx.org
#menopauseatwork #perimenopause #womenshealth #womenatwork #menopause

scenes.text: Hot flash mid-*presentation*. She felt like the problem.
scenes.suggest: → Ask HR *in writing*: fan + flex hours (Fawcett 2022)

scenes.text: At 49 she kept her blazer on to hide the sweat, and said nothing.
phrases: Are you okay? You look flushed.
Maybe sit out the client pitch?
She's been tired lately, that's all.
She wasn't tired. She was 49, and nobody had said the word menopause.

scenes.text: 1 in 10 UK women who worked through menopause *left a job* because of symptoms.
She asked HR for a desk fan and a 9:30 start. Both came back approved.
phrases: She wrote six lines to HR on a Tuesday.
A desk fan. A 9:30 start. That was it.
Both were approved inside a week.
Flexibility and temperature control are what women ask for most (Fawcett, 2022).

scenes.text: Tonight: send one written line naming the exact change you want at work.
phrases: Tonight: one email to HR naming the exact change you want.
Most weeks: 150 minutes of moderate movement (WHO, 2020).
Small asks, put in writing, are the ones that get approved.
